reviews.title: not reliable or accurate

reviews.title: So…

I have had a few different animal, insect and plant identifier apps over the past 5 years or so and this one this app is great.. for comic relief!! I took a picture of three newborn baby rabbits just to gain some extra knowledge on them. The image came back as american toads. I then took a closer shot from about 3 inches away and it only reached a much… MUCH wilder level of high strange crazy and returned with a identifier of HUMAN! Three baby rabbits… HUMANS?!?!? From a few inches away??? Thats where I draw the line..

reviews.title: Why does everything use AI
reviews.text: I used to get relatively accurate plant identification from this app. At some point in the recent past, they switched to an AI that could not accurately identify a plant if it was reading a label. I went from correctly identifying plants 9 times out of 10 to identifying a plum tree as a wasp. There were no wasps in the picture. There were hanging plums in the picture. At no point did it identify the plant as a tree, the fruit as a plum, or anything even remotely accurate. I’m deleting this app. I wish that everything that used to be helpful had not become so reliant on the use of AI to fix problems that didn’t exist in the first place.

reviews.title: Hate that I have to hate it.
reviews.text:
So much is great about this app. It’s user friendly, the id model is remarkable and reliable. I just hate that it is such an invasion of privacy. It requires you to give access to your location, and doesn’t allow you to save any other options such as location or geoprivacy. If you don’t allow location access then it forces you to choose your location on a map EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. It is incredibly tedious and frustrating and done so deliberately so people give in and allow access. Unfortunately when you have to select it, the location starts out in the wrong area and soon people will just hit okay to get through the process faster rather than select an area that encompasses the spot you took the picture at. I hope they fix this, the other plant id apps are catching up.



Taking off a star because of you leave one star the devs can delete it. If you don’t give them access to your location and choose to do it manually they nerf the app and you can no longer get ids.


Also for the love of plants stop making us go through that stupid reminder every time we open the camera, put a box that we can check saying that we understand and make it so we don’t have to see it every single time

reviews.title: Spoiled by AI Slop
reviews.text:
This app was 4.5/5 before the most recent update. Now I can’t get a single accurate response. 50% of my finds are “human” because my hand is in the photo (holding the flower or bug) or the AI picks up one of several species around the one I’m trying to nab (already a problem before, but much worse now), OR it’ll just completely and obviously miss the mark. A clear picture of a praying mantis turned up 3 different beetles and a type of ant before landing on a (incorrect) species of mantis. 

Disappointing for such a wonderful app.

reviews.title: Cannot identify things

This is particularly problematic now that it was working a few seasons ago, but now cannot identify common things like live oaks. Point it at a native grass and it barely recognizes it as a grass. Point it at a block of concrete and it tells you it is a bird.

reviews.title: Worse than ever, sadly
reviews.text: I have used this app for years, and I love ID-ing plants, birds, animals. I’ve recommended it to countless people in the past, but with the newer AI powered version, it’s not doing great. Today it told me that ducks (with green heads) were a “canada goose”. Yesterday it claimed a pelican (with a trademark long pelican beak) was a “common merganser”. I have been using it to check invasive plants in my yard, and it’s misidentifying those as well. I thought it would get better over time but this is embarrassing… I miss its former reliability.

reviews.title: Almost there!
reviews.text:
This app does a lot of cool stuff! There are two reasons I don’t use it:
- The initial safety “Remember screen” is not safe at all and a poor design choice. At least provide a setting to turn it off! I appreciate the warning and fully agree it should be there a few times, but not as a persistent message. This has the unintended effect of drawing a person’s awareness away from nature and into the app, ironically leading to them becoming less aware of their surroundings. App deloading can make this an even more frustrating experience especially when low power mode leads to that occurring more, compounded with this being more common for people going on long hikes, and even further since people that are into long hikes could also be more into Seeking things as they go along which drains battery further and thus low power mode. 
- It should give a link to the species after identification to quickly get to more details about the capture. This could be a direct link to Wikipedia or a prebuilt Google search link, anything to just get the species name easier into a place it can be searched for. EDIT: the link does exist, but only if you are logged into iNaturalist
- On the species page, why can you not view other photos of the plant fullscreen?!
